/-!
# Conjecture 10.12

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Does there exist a finitely generated cancellative semigroup of non-exponential
growth whose group of left quotients exists and has exponential growth?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.12»

open Filter GromovPolynomialGrowth

/-- The elements of a semigroup `S` represented by nonempty words of length at
most `n` in `A`. The products are evaluated in an ambient group because a
semigroup need not contain an identity element. -/
def semigroupBall {G : Type*} [Group G] (S : Subsemigroup G) (A : Set S)
    (n : ℕ) : Set S :=
  {s | ∃ l : List S, l ≠ [] ∧ l.length ≤ n ∧ (∀ x ∈ l, x ∈ A) ∧
    (l.map fun x ↦ (x : G)).prod = (s : G)}

/-- The upper exponential growth rate of a function `f`, namely
$\limsup_{n \to \infty} f(n)^{1/n}$. -/
noncomputable def exponentialGrowthRate (f : ℕ → ℕ) : ℝ :=
  limsup (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ) ^ (1 / (n : ℝ))) atTop

/--
Does there exist a finitely generated semigroup $S$ with cancellation and
non-exponential growth such that its group of left quotients
$G = S^{-1}S$ exists and has exponential growth?

Here `S : Subsemigroup G` records the cancellative semigroup together with its
embedding in the quotient group. The final condition on `g` states that every
element of $G$ has the form $s^{-1}t$. The finite set $A$ generates $S$ as a
semigroup. Non-exponential and exponential growth mean that the respective
exponential growth rates are equal to $1$ and greater than $1$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.12» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (S : Subsemigroup G) (A : Set S),
      A.Finite ∧ Subsemigroup.closure A = ⊤ ∧
      exponentialGrowthRate (fun n ↦ (semigroupBall S A n).ncard) = 1 ∧
      exponentialGrowthRate (GrowthFunction ((fun s : S ↦ (s : G)) '' A)) > 1 ∧
      ∀ g : G, ∃ s t : S, g = (s : G)⁻¹ * (t : G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.12»
modeling_decisions: Model the cancellative semigroup together with its injective embedding as a `Subsemigroup G`; cancellation is inherited from the ambient group.

Express that `G` is precisely the group of left quotients by requiring every `g : G` to have the form `(s : G)⁻¹ * (t : G)` for `s t : S`. Together with the embedding, this captures the left Ore quotient-group hypothesis.

Use one finite semigroup generating set `A : Set S`. Semigroup growth counts products of nonempty words of length at most `n`; group growth uses the repository's symmetric `GromovPolynomialGrowth.GrowthFunction` on the image of the same generators.
Interpret non-exponential and exponential growth as upper exponential growth rate respectively equal to `1` and strictly greater than `1`, using the standard limsup of nth roots.

/-!
# Conjecture 10.12

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Does there exist a finitely generated cancellative semigroup of non-exponential growth whose
existing group of left quotients has exponential growth?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.12»

open Filter

/-- The elements of a semigroup expressible as products of between one and $n$ elements of
`A`. -/
def semigroupBall {S : Type*} [Semigroup S] (A : Finset S) (n : ℕ) : Set S :=
  {x | ∃ w : FreeSemigroup {a // a ∈ A}, w.length ≤ n ∧
    FreeSemigroup.lift (fun a => (a : S)) w = x}

/-- The exponential growth rate of a semigroup with respect to a finite set `A`. -/
noncomputable def semigroupGrowthRate {S : Type*} [Semigroup S] (A : Finset S) : ℝ :=
  limsup (fun n : ℕ => ((semigroupBall A n).ncard : ℝ) ^ (1 / (n : ℝ))) atTop

/-- A finitely generated semigroup has subexponential growth if its exponential growth rate is
one with respect to a finite semigroup generating set. -/
def HasSubexponentialGrowth (S : Type*) [Semigroup S] : Prop :=
  ∃ A : Finset S, Subsemigroup.closure (A : Set S) = ⊤ ∧ semigroupGrowthRate A = 1

/-- The elements of a group expressible as words of length at most $n$ in `A` and their
inverses. -/
def groupBall {G : Type*} [Group G] (A : Finset G) (n : ℕ) : Set G :=
  {x | ∃ w : FreeMonoid ({a // a ∈ A} × Bool), w.length ≤ n ∧
    FreeMonoid.lift (fun a : {a // a ∈ A} × Bool => if a.2 then (a.1 : G)⁻¹ else a.1) w = x}

/-- The exponential growth rate of a group with respect to a finite set `A`, using `A` and its
inverses as letters. -/
noncomputable def groupGrowthRate {G : Type*} [Group G] (A : Finset G) : ℝ :=
  limsup (fun n : ℕ => ((groupBall A n).ncard : ℝ) ^ (1 / (n : ℝ))) atTop

/-- A finitely generated group has exponential growth if its exponential growth rate is strictly
greater than one with respect to a finite group generating set. -/
def HasExponentialGrowth (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ A : Finset G, Subgroup.closure (A : Set G) = ⊤ ∧ 1 < groupGrowthRate A

/-- A group `G` is a group of left quotients of a semigroup `S` via `ι` if `ι` is an embedding and
every element of `G` has the form $\iota(s)^{-1}\iota(t)$. -/
def IsGroupOfLeftQuotients {S G : Type*} [Semigroup S] [Group G] (ι : S →ₙ* G) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective ι ∧ ∀ g : G, ∃ s t : S, g = (ι s)⁻¹ * ι t

/--
Does there exist a finitely generated semigroup $S$ with cancellation and non-exponential growth
such that its group of left quotients $G=S^{-1}S$ (which exists) has exponential growth?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.12» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (S : Type) (_ : Semigroup S) (_ : IsCancelMul S),
      HasSubexponentialGrowth S ∧
      ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (ι : S →ₙ* G),
        IsGroupOfLeftQuotients ι ∧ HasExponentialGrowth G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.12»
modeling_decisions: A finitely generated semigroup has non-exponential growth when the limsup of the nth roots of its positive-word ball cardinalities is 1 for a finite semigroup generating set, as specified by the decomposition.
A group's word balls use a finite subgroup generating set together with the inverses of its elements; exponential growth means that the corresponding limsup nth-root rate is strictly greater than 1.

Existence of the group of left quotients is represented by an injective semigroup homomorphism into a group such that every group element equals ι(s)⁻¹ * ι(t). This keeps S a genuine semigroup rather than strengthening it to a monoid.
Two-sided cancellation is represented by Mathlib's IsCancelMul typeclass.

/-!
# Conjecture 10.12

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Does there exist a finitely generated semigroup $S$ with cancellation having
non-exponential growth and such that its group of left quotients $G = S^{-1}S$
(which exists) is a group of exponential growth?

The notebook remarks that an affirmative answer would give a positive solution to
Problem 12 in S. Wagon, *The Banach–Tarski Paradox*, Cambridge Univ. Press, 1985.

Here $S$ is a two-sided cancellative semigroup. Its group of left quotients is a group
$G$ containing $S$ (up to an embedding) such that every element of $G$ has the form
$s^{-1}t$ with $s, t \in S$. The growth function of $S$ with respect to a finite
generating set $A$ counts the elements of $S$ that are products of at most $n$
elements of $A$. Non-exponential growth means $\lim_n \gamma_A(n)^{1/n} = 1$;
exponential growth of $G$ means $\lim_n \gamma_T(n)^{1/n} > 1$ for a finite generating
set $T$ of $G$. Both notions are independent of the finite generating set.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.12»

open Filter GromovPolynomialGrowth

variable {S : Type*} [Semigroup S]

/-- The ball of radius `n` in the semigroup `S` with respect to `A`: the elements of `S`
that are products of at least one and at most `n` elements of `A`. -/
def semigroupBall (A : Set S) (n : ℕ) : Set S :=
  {x | ∃ w : FreeSemigroup A, w.length ≤ n ∧ FreeSemigroup.lift Subtype.val w = x}

/-- The growth function of the semigroup `S` with respect to `A` counts the elements
of `S` that are products of at least one and at most `n` elements of `A`. -/
noncomputable def semigroupGrowthFunction (A : Set S) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (semigroupBall A n).ncard

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem semigroupBall_zero (A : Set S) : semigroupBall A 0 = ∅ := by
  ext x
  simp only [semigroupBall, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false, not_exists,
    not_and]
  intro w hw
  simp [FreeSemigroup.length] at hw

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem semigroupBall_one (A : Set S) : semigroupBall A 1 = A := by
  ext x
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩
    induction w using FreeSemigroup.recOnMul with
    | ih1 a => simp
    | ih2 w₁ w₂ _ _ =>
      simp [FreeSemigroup.length] at hw
  · intro hx
    exact ⟨FreeSemigroup.of ⟨x, hx⟩, le_rfl, rfl⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem semigroupBall_mono (A : Set S) {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) :
    semigroupBall A m ⊆ semigroupBall A n :=
  fun _ ⟨w, hw, hx⟩ => ⟨w, hw.trans h, hx⟩

/-- A finitely generated semigroup `S` has non-exponential (subexponential) growth if it
has a finite generating set `A` whose growth function satisfies $\gamma_A(n) \le c^n$ for
all large $n$, for every $c > 1$; that is, $\lim_n \gamma_A(n)^{1/n} = 1$. This property
does not depend on the choice of finite generating set. -/
def HasSubexponentialGrowth (S : Type*) [Semigroup S] : Prop :=
  ∃ A : Set S, A.Finite ∧ Subsemigroup.closure A = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ c : ℝ, 1 < c → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (semigroupGrowthFunction A n : ℝ) ≤ c ^ n

/-- A finitely generated group `G` has exponential growth if it has a finite generating
set `T` whose growth function satisfies $\gamma_T(n) \ge c^n$ for all large $n$, for some
$c > 1$; that is, $\lim_n \gamma_T(n)^{1/n} > 1$. This property does not depend on the
choice of finite generating set. -/
def HasExponentialGrowth (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set G, T.Finite ∧ Subgroup.closure T = ⊤ ∧
    ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c ^ n ≤ (GrowthFunction T n : ℝ)

/-- A semigroup homomorphism `φ : S → G` into a group `G` makes `G` the group of left
quotients $G = S^{-1}S$ of `S` if `φ` is injective (so `S` embeds into `G`) and every
element of `G` has the form $\varphi(s)^{-1}\varphi(t)$ with $s, t \in S$. -/
def IsGroupOfLeftQuotients {G : Type*} [Group G] (φ : S →ₙ* G) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective φ ∧ ∀ g : G, ∃ s t : S, g = (φ s)⁻¹ * φ t

/--
Does there exist a finitely generated semigroup $S$ with cancellation having
non-exponential growth and such that its group of left quotients $G = S^{-1}S$
(which exists) is a group of exponential growth?

The existence of the group of left quotients is part of the hypothesis: it is
formalised as the existence of a group $G$ and an injective semigroup homomorphism
$\varphi : S \to G$ with $G = \varphi(S)^{-1}\varphi(S)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.12» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (S : Type) (_ : Semigroup S) (_ : IsCancelMul S) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (φ : S →ₙ* G),
      HasSubexponentialGrowth S ∧ IsGroupOfLeftQuotients φ ∧ HasExponentialGrowth G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.12»

(which exists) is a group of exponential growth?

growth) does not depend on the finite generating set. The same holds for the
growth function of a finitely generated group (`GromovPolynomialGrowth.GrowthFunction`).

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- S. Wagon, *The Banach–Tarski Paradox*, Cambridge Univ. Press, 1985.
-/

/-!
# Conjecture 10.12

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Does there exist a finitely generated cancellative semigroup of non-exponential growth whose
(existing) group of left quotients has exponential growth?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.12»

/-- The ball of radius $n$ in a semigroup with generating set $A$: the products of between one
and $n$ elements of $A$. -/
def wordBall {M : Type*} [Semigroup M] (A : Set M) (n : ℕ) : Set M :=
  {x | ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ l : List M, l.length < n ∧ (∀ b ∈ l, b ∈ A) ∧
    l.foldl (· * ·) a = x}

/-- The exponential growth rate of the word balls of a semigroup with respect to a generating
set. -/
noncomputable def growthRate {M : Type*} [Semigroup M] (A : Set M) : ℝ :=
  Filter.atTop.limsup fun n : ℕ => Real.rpow (wordBall A n).ncard (1 / (n : ℝ))

/--
Does there exist a finitely generated semigroup $S$ with cancellation and non-exponential growth
such that its group of left quotients $G=S^{-1}S$ exists and has exponential growth?

Here `i` embeds $S$ in $G$, and the condition on every $g : G$ says precisely that every element
of $G$ is a left quotient $i(s)^{-1}i(t)$. The finite set $A$ semigroup-generates $S$.
Non-exponential growth means that its exponential growth rate is $1$; the rate for $G$ is computed
using the symmetric generating set consisting of the images of $A$ and their inverses.
-/

theorem kourovka.«10.12» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (S : Type) (_ : Semigroup S) (_ : LeftCancelSemigroup S) (_ : RightCancelSemigroup S)
      (A : Set S), A.Finite ∧ Subsemigroup.closure A = ⊤ ∧ growthRate A = 1 ∧
      ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (i : S →ₙ* G), Function.Injective i ∧
        (∀ g : G, ∃ s t : S, g = (i s)⁻¹ * i t) ∧
        1 < growthRate (i '' A ∪ (fun g : G => g⁻¹) '' (i '' A)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.12»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.12

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Does there exist a finitely generated semigroup $S$ with cancellation having non-exponential
growth and such that its group of left quotients $G = S^{-1}S$ (which exists) is a group of
exponential growth?

The notebook remarks that an affirmative answer would give a positive solution to Problem 12 in
S. Wagon, *The Banach–Tarski Paradox*, Cambridge Univ. Press, 1985.

The growth function of a semigroup $S$ with respect to a finite generating set $A$ counts the
elements of $S$ that are products of at most $n$ elements of $A$. The growth function of a group
$G$ with respect to a finite generating set $B$ counts the elements of $G$ that are products of at
most $n$ elements of $B \cup B^{-1}$ (see `GromovPolynomialGrowth.GrowthFunction`). In both cases
the limit $\lim_{n \to \infty} \gamma(n)^{1/n}$ exists, and the growth is called *exponential* if
this limit is $> 1$ and *non-exponential* (subexponential) if it equals $1$; this does not depend
on the choice of the finite generating set.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open Filter GromovPolynomialGrowth
open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«10.12»

variable {S : Type*} [Semigroup S]

/-- `semigroupBall A n` is the set of elements of the semigroup `S` that can be written as a
product of at least one and at most `n` elements of `A`. -/
def semigroupBall (A : Set S) : ℕ → Set S
  | 0 => ∅
  | n + 1 => A ∪ semigroupBall A n * A

/-- The growth function of the semigroup `S` with respect to `A`: the number of elements of `S`
that can be written as a product of at most `n` elements of `A`. -/
noncomputable def semigroupGrowthFunction (A : Set S) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (semigroupBall A n).ncard

/-- A semigroup has *non-exponential* (subexponential) growth with respect to a finite generating
set `A` if its growth function $\gamma_A$ satisfies $\gamma_A(n) \le c^n$ for all large $n$, for
every $c > 1$; equivalently $\lim_{n \to \infty} \gamma_A(n)^{1/n} = 1$. -/
def HasSubexponentialGrowth (A : Set S) : Prop :=
  ∀ c : ℝ, 1 < c → ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (semigroupGrowthFunction A n : ℝ) ≤ c ^ n

/-- A group `G` has *exponential growth* with respect to a finite generating set `B` if its growth
function $\gamma_B$ satisfies $\gamma_B(n) \ge c^n$ for all large $n$, for some $c > 1$;
equivalently $\lim_{n \to \infty} \gamma_B(n)^{1/n} > 1$. -/
def HasExponentialGrowth {G : Type*} [Group G] (B : Set G) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, c ^ n ≤ (GrowthFunction B n : ℝ)

/-- The ball of radius `0` is empty: a semigroup has no empty products. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem semigroupBall_zero (A : Set S) : semigroupBall A 0 = ∅ := by
  simp [semigroupBall]

/-- The ball of radius `1` is the generating set itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem semigroupBall_one (A : Set S) : semigroupBall A 1 = A := by
  simp [semigroupBall]

/-- The ball of radius `2` consists of the generators and the products of two generators. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem semigroupBall_two (A : Set S) : semigroupBall A 2 = A ∪ A * A := by
  simp [semigroupBall]

/--
Does there exist a finitely generated semigroup $S$ with cancellation having non-exponential
growth and such that its group of left quotients $G = S^{-1}S$ (which exists) is a group of
exponential growth?

Here $S$ is a (two-sided) cancellative semigroup generated by a finite set $A$. Its group of left
quotients is a group $G$ together with an injective semigroup homomorphism $\varphi : S \to G$
such that every element of $G$ has the form $\varphi(s)^{-1} \varphi(t)$ with $s, t \in S$; the
existence of $G$ (equivalent to the left Ore condition $Sa \cap Sb \ne \emptyset$ for all
$a, b \in S$) is part of the hypothesis, and $G$ is unique up to isomorphism. The group $G$ is
generated by $\varphi(A)$, and its growth is measured with respect to this finite generating set;
having exponential (resp. non-exponential) growth does not depend on the choice of finite
generating set.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.12» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (S : Type) (_ : Semigroup S) (_ : IsCancelMul S) (A : Finset S),
      Subsemigroup.closure (A : Set S) = ⊤ ∧ HasSubexponentialGrowth (A : Set S) ∧
      ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (φ : S →ₙ* G), Function.Injective φ ∧
        (∀ g : G, ∃ s t : S, g = (φ s)⁻¹ * φ t) ∧ HasExponentialGrowth (⇑φ '' (A : Set S)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.12»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (left Ore condition as hypothesis via embedding with G = S⁻¹S, growth rate 1 vs > 1, remark about Wagon's Problem 12 not being a further question) are correct and were followed.
modeling_decisions: Cancellation is stated as IsCancelMul S (two-sided). It is mathematically redundant given the injective homomorphism into a group, but kept because the statement says 'with cancellation'.

The group of left quotients is modeled as ∃ G group, φ : S →ₙ* G injective, with every g = (φ s)⁻¹ * φ t (G = S⁻¹S literally). Since the group of left quotients is unique up to isomorphism, the existential quantification over G is equivalent to a universal one over all such G, and growth type is an isomorphism invariant.

Growth of S is measured w.r.t. the chosen finite generating set A (∃ A); growth of G is measured w.r.t. φ '' A, which generates G as a group (every element is φ(s)⁻¹φ(t) with s, t products of elements of A). Both exponential and non-exponential growth are independent of the finite generating set, so this is faithful; a reviewer may prefer an ∃/∀ over generating sets of G instead.

Semigroup ball = products of 1..n generators (no empty product); the group growth function (repo's GrowthFunction/CayleyBall) uses words of length ≤ n in B ∪ B⁻¹ including the identity. These conventions differ by bounded amounts and do not affect exponential vs. subexponential.

'Non-exponential' is formalized as subexponential (∀ c > 1, eventually γ(n) ≤ c^n, i.e. limsup γ(n)^{1/n} ≤ 1) and 'exponential' as ∃ c > 1, eventually c^n ≤ γ(n) (liminf > 1). Since the ball growth functions are (essentially) submultiplicative, lim γ(n)^{1/n} exists and the two notions are complementary, so this is the same as '¬ exponential'.
Degenerate case: an empty S satisfies closure ∅ = ⊤, but then no group G can satisfy ∀ g, ∃ s t : S, g = (φ s)⁻¹ * φ t, so it does not give a spurious witness.

Three short proven @[category API] lemmas (semigroupBall at radius 0, 1, 2) are included as basic API tests for the bespoke definition, per CONTRIBUTING.md; the slot itself is exactly one declaration kourovka.«10.12».
